sections.title: Authority and scope
sections.content: The self-hosted trust-recovery plan consumes repository rules, lifecycle and Knowledge ADRs, Skill contracts, consumer policy, requirements, implementation contract, command registry, terminal validator, and the persisted Acceptance run owner. Lifecycle ownership remains: Maintainer publishes implementation authorization, Quick Dev owns implementation completion, and Acceptance owns acceptance passage. Bootstrap startup, Knowledge publication, runtime or deployment changes, historical-plan mutation, and trust signing are not authorized.

sections.title: Repair constraints
sections.content: Repair round 1 is limited to terminal compatibility, final receipt bindings, traceability, self-hosted authority declarations, protection of the immutable 2026-08-17 plan, and correction of the RED baseline. Pre-existing shared workflow changes are outside slice write sets and require separate ownership or explicit disposition before plan-ready. Repair closure remains absent pending validation and maintainer prerequisites.

sections.title: Execution slices
sections.content: R0 establishes a binding-derived persisted Acceptance evidence root and rejects request-local authority or incompletely bound receipts. R1 makes successor creation reentrant through an identical reservation and fails closed on conflicting identity. R2 preserves authorization across verified, same-selection Knowledge refreshes while routing selection or execution-semantics drift to reauthorization. R3 verifies legacy prior-RED evidence only when selector, test bytes, execution fingerprint, and expected failure IDs match. R4 performs a read-only replay of 2026-08-17 evidence while producing fresh current bindings.

sections.title: Knowledge continuity
sections.content: A refresh may replay a frozen selection from a verified published or last-known-good catalog when selection, scope, resource semantics, policy, contract, commands, tests, and authority remain unchanged. Ordinary catalog staleness or selected source-byte drift may yield degraded execution through one validated successor. Invalid or tampered LKG data, missing required sources, selection or authority drift, and Knowledge-system self-change with a failed query gate remain blocking. Acceptance and Quick Dev may consume successor context but cannot publish Knowledge authority or rewrite maintainer authorization.

sections.title: Validation and completion
sections.content: The registry defines slice GREEN commands, per-slice terminal commands, full Quick Dev and Acceptance suites, and a terminal-full command. The terminal validator checks maintainer authorization, Knowledge freeze binding, current Skill-input receipt validation, registered test commands, candidate identity, and final artifact hashes. Slice predicates are slice-ready; the full predicate is implementation-complete. Results are non-authorizing and record no lifecycle transition.
